A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPORT, with matching authors, algorithms, benchmarks and principal results despite the changed title. The main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison; no material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: v1 reports original GTA and GAIA evaluations, iteration and preference-data ablations, analyses of generated steps, and human evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds initialization and diversity ablations, a task-generator comparison, computational estimates and repeated-run reporting.

M1.justification: The ReAct controller, four-stage SPORT loop, best-step selection, preference-pair construction and DPO objective are retained. v4 expands implementation documentation for task generation, including revision and filtering, without establishing an algorithmic replacement. Testing SPORT without MAT initialization is presented as an ablation.

E1.justification: Both retain GTA and GAIA evaluation, MAT-seeded task synthesis and MM-Traj-based training comparisons. v4 identifies ShareGPT4V as the image-retrieval source without establishing newly expanded coverage. Its additional model and seed-count experiments and illustrative cases remain within the existing multimodal tool-use setting.

E2.justification: v4 Table 1 omits four Lego Agent configurations reported in v1: GPT-3.5-turbo, Claude3-opus, Qwen1.5-72B-chat and LLaMA3-70B-instruct. It also removes the GAIA Sibyl/GPT-4-turbo comparison. The central HF, T3-Agent and MAT-SFT-DPO comparisons remain; Warm-up Agent matches the earlier Warm-up Act.

E3.justification: v4 adds GTA controls with and without MAT initialization, 5 examples/100 seeds versus 20 examples/425 seeds, and an anonymized 400-task generator study with 20 evaluators. It describes d as a trajectory count rather than v1 Section 3.4's preference-pair count; unchanged retained scores do not establish reruns. Disabling sampling and verification at inference is newly disclosed, not demonstrated to be a changed setting.

E4.justification: The original iteration-size and static-preference-data ablations remain. v4 substantially extends the questions investigated through initialization and task-diversity ablations, open-versus-closed task-generator evaluation, computational-efficiency analysis, and three additional case studies involving image editing, snack prices and fruit localization.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without repeated-run information. v4 Appendix E first states five repetitions per experiment and supplies variability for SPORT's three GTA metrics, including 60.26 ± 1.51 AnsAcc. Baseline and GAIA uncertainty are not displayed, and no significance test is specified. This newly reported run count does not establish an increase over v1.

E6.justification: The original SPORT benchmark scores remain 60.26% GTA AnsAcc and 20.61% GAIA AnsAcc. v4 adds configuration-specific results such as 55.13% without MAT initialization and 58.33% with reduced seed diversity, plus generator-quality scores and computational estimates in Tables 9–10. Some baseline results disappear. The new Table 4 discussion incorrectly calls 60.26 minus 53.85 a 5.13-point gain; the table implies 6.41 points.

T1.justification: The ReAct selection equations, m(n−1) preference-pair construction and DPO loss retain their mathematical substance. Replacing solution notation with action notation and clarifying training-batch bookkeeping introduce no new theoretical result. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v4 focuses the framing on tool-usage exploration and makes the 16K preference dataset an explicit contribution; v1 already reported constructing and using 16K pairs. The annotation-free exploration claim and claimed 6.41- and 3.64-point benchmark improvements remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the added experiments as supporting independence from MAT initialization, resilience to reduced task diversity and the adequacy of open-source generators. It attributes efficiency gains mainly to smaller data-generation workloads and clarifies that verification judges useful tool outcomes rather than their truth. Appendix A replaces the generic impact statement with specific risks of reinforcing hallucinations and spurious behavior; the original prompt-dependent-verifier limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendices D and F disclose the image source, query/file-generation prompts, query-file revision and filtering, and associated implementation instructions absent from v1. v4 also supplies hardware, component timing, model-role information and inference-time search settings. Conversely, v1's explicit four-iteration training statement is omitted. The project link remains equivalent; a new public data release is not established.

R1.justification: v4 adds Search-R1 and ReTool when discussing correctness-reward-based tool learning, alongside newer multimodal-agent references and ShareGPT4V. References including SeeClick, Sibyl and VioTGPT disappear. The existing SFT/RL, step-wise preference and AI-feedback positioning and sampling-framework comparison largely remain; publication-metadata updates are not new cited works.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around tool usage, and the contributions and challenge discussion are reorganized. Solution terminology becomes action terminology throughout much of the method. GAIA results move before the ablations, related-work prose is compressed, and the appendix structure is extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two-column to single-column layout. The separate GTA and GAIA tables are merged, Figure 2 is redrawn, and the qualitative diagrams receive revised formatting and annotations. New ablation, timing, generator-quality and uncertainty tables, prompt boxes and case-study figures are added. The old code-error table disappears, while its values remain in prose.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility and evidential support through task-generation instructions, targeted initialization/diversity ablations, a generator-quality study and GTA variability reporting absent from v1. These gains are moderated by removed comparator rows, unspecified significance testing, and efficiency estimates comparing different workloads without clearly accounting for the MAT warm-start. The new incorrect gain statement beside Table 4 also weakens precision. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
